original_card.question: Can one specified masked or overcomplete decoder improve the complete moment budget?
methods: Synthesize a decoder with exact coefficients and fully priced helper endpoints.
Bound the best possible budget for a fixed support alphabet before synthesis.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound and count all copied information, frames and restoration.

first_step.inspect: Locate the excluded classes: masked identities, at least nine terms, and deeper punctures.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose one finite support alphabet and test exact decoding constraints before building a whole network.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A cheaper fully realized decoder could increase deficit or lower recursive cost on the binding complex side.
allowed_variations: Select a specific masked or overcomplete family with exact labels and supports.
scope_change_triggers: Repeating the exact eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: Proof-obligation reduction inside the masked (E-graph) model: for every 5-subset X of P112 not inside a P112 frame (1607 orbits under the 8-generator FRAME0-stabiliser subgroup by make_units.py's census; the frame-contained ones are PR1419's), is there a pivot frame F inside P112 \ X that passes every per-unit input of the PR1212/PR1399 rigidity method other than (I2) zero exclusion, namely (I3) with live witnesses, (I4) on all 14 blocks, gluing, and Lemma 9 connectivity with its sign identity and rank-3 algebra?
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a masked decoder can beat the floor. The rank-8 line (PR1212, PR1389, PR1399, PR1419, PR1425, PR1469, PR1474) answers it for exactly eight costly terms down to P108. an664 claimed the structural (I2) lemma toward P107 in discussion 1502, so this package takes only the complementary non-(I2) part at P107 and does not touch zero exclusion. It constructs no decoder.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the binding complex supplier: with it, a structural (I2) zero-exclusion lemma for the listed pivots would extend PR968's floor 59 for masked eight-costly-term decoders to every P107 unit; no unit is blocked by the other inputs.
stop_rule: Stop at P107 with the non-(I2) inputs; (I2), P106-P105 and nine or more costly terms are left open.
evidence: verify.py: 7 exact checks in about 2.6 minutes (generators; triple orbits; two-level candidate coverage with explicit generator words, 2517 quadruple candidates onto 180 representatives and 18710 open 5-subset candidates onto 1607 units; a control that the first frame inside the live set fails on u0001; per unit the pivot's D4 structure, (I3), (I4), gluing, Lemma 9 connectivity, sign identity and rank-3 algebra, and the section 7 assembly identity). make_units.py checked once that the 1614 5-subset orbit sizes sum to C(112,5) = 134153712 (census, not needed by the argument). A read-only adversarial review by OpenAI Codex found no soundness gap (not a human review).
author: JosieElliston (with Claude Opus 5.5 via Claude Code)
ai_assistance: Claude Opus 5.5 via Claude Code: census, pivot search, verifier and write-up. OpenAI Codex: read-only adversarial review. Submitted by the account holder.

open_questions.question: (I2) zero exclusion on the 1607 (unit, pivot) pairs of UNITS.json, by a structural lemma rather than per-orbit DRUP certificates.
open_questions.why_it_matters: With this package it is the only per-unit input left at P107; with PR1419's Lemma 10 it would give every P107 unit and PR968's floor 59.
open_questions.first_step: an664's discussion 1502 claim targets exactly this; check there first. Otherwise test whether the trans and diag families alone refute a zero on these pivots.
open_questions.blocked_by: No structural (I2) lemma is known; per-orbit DRUP would cost on the order of 50 MB here.

open_questions.question: Do the non-(I2) inputs survive at P106 and P105 (P112 minus 6-7 lines outside a frame)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: PR968's floor goes to p = 15 (P105). If some unit has no passing pivot there, no (I2) lemma alone can close it with this method.
open_questions.first_step: Rerun make_units.py one level deeper: candidates are P107 orbit representatives plus one line, keyed by their sub-5-subset canonical forms.
open_questions.blocked_by: Orbit counts grow toward order 1e4 at P106 and 1e5 at P105; the pivot search (about 0.1 s per frame) needs a better pivot order or a counting argument.
